targets.problem: Removing iron from secondary (scrap) aluminium melts continuously and economically, so recycled alloy can meet wrought/automotive specs without dilution by primary metal. Iron accumulates to ~1-2 wt% across recycling loops and forms brittle plate-like beta-AlFeSi needles; current best lab routes (high-shear melt conditioning plus gravity sedimentation of primary Al-Fe-Mn-Si polyhedra) hit ~90% removal in BATCH but only ~60% CONTINUOUS. The specific stuck sub-problem: a continuous-flow settling/filtration unit, and the melt chemistry (Mn/Cr/Si/Be ratios, superheat-and-hold schedule) that reliably forces Fe into dense compact alpha phases rather than buoyant platelets.
targets.notes: B-terms to bridge through: 'sludge' / 'sludge factor' (the die-casting term for the exact same Fe-Mn-Cr primary intermetallic sediment that founders spent 1930-1980 trying to AVOID in holding furnaces — an enormous applied literature on how to make it form fast and settle, read backwards); 'segregation freezing' / 'fractional crystallisation' / 'Hoopes cell' / 'three-layer refining'; 'gravity segregation in holding furnaces'; 'Al-Si sludge formation', 'hard spots', 'furnace bottom build-up', 'iron pick-up from tools'; boron and beryllium 'iron correctors'; 'cineritic'/Soviet 'otstaivanie' (settling) and 'zonnaya plavka'. OLD vocabulary note: pre-1985 nobody said 'recycling' or 'circular' — say 'secondary aluminium', 'remelt', 'dross', 'skimmings', 'low-grade pig'. Literatures to dig: AFS Transactions and Modern Casting 1940-1980; Journal of Metals / Light Metals (AIME) 1950s; US Bureau of Mines RI reports on secondary aluminium (huge, grey, barely indexed); Aluminium (Dusseldorf) and Tsvetnye Metally in translation; patent class for 'purification of aluminium alloys'. TRAP for a scout: do not return modern (post-2010) high-shear/LiME-Hub papers as finds — they are the state of the art the target is about. Also beware Be-containing recipes (toxic, non-startable) and 'add primary metal' answers (that IS the problem). || WHY OLD LIT: The die-casting industry spent five decades characterising exactly which melt chemistries and thermal holds precipitate dense Fe-Mn-Cr sludge, because sludge ruined their castings. That is the same phase modern recyclers are trying to deliberately nucleate and settle, so a whole negative-results literature is sitting there as a positive recipe book under a word ('sludge') that no recycling paper searches on. The Bureau of Mines also ran continuous secondary-aluminium pilot work in the 1960s-70s under energy/strategic-materials programs that was shelved when primary metal got cheap; those reports are paper-only and almost absent from the modern citation graph. || HOW TO CHECK: Cheap and decisive. A surviving lead is a specified melt chemistry plus thermal/stirring schedule: run it as a 5-20 kg induction-melt trial, hold at the stated superheat and temperature, sample top and bottom, measure Fe by OES or ICP and identify phases by SEM/EDS and XRD. Weeks, a few thousand dollars at any casting lab or university foundry; also pre-screenable for free against Thermo-Calc/CALPHAD Al-Fe-Mn-Si-Cr equilibria before touching a furnace.

targets.problem: A coating that protects niobium/tantalum/molybdenum and refractory high-entropy alloys through the 'pest' regime (roughly 600-925 C, catastrophic oxygen-driven disintegration on thermal cycling) AND up to 1300-1500 C, surviving hundreds of cycles and low-pressure/water-vapour-bearing flows. Modern work (HAPC/SAPS silicides, MoSi2 outer layers) gets good isothermal numbers at 1200-1500 C but the open failures are long-term thermal cycling across the pest window, Nb2O5-SiO2 eutectic melting, and active SiO/Si(OH)4 volatilisation at low pO2. This is now rate-limiting for hypersonic leading edges and for refractory-HEA turbine hardware.
targets.notes: B-terms: 'pest' / 'pesting' / 'Pestbefall' (German) / 'low-temperature catastrophic oxidation'; 'Durak-B', 'Durak-KA', 'R512E', 'R512A', 'Vac-Hyd', 'Sylvania', 'TRW Cr-Ti-Si', 'LB-2', 'Disil'; 'slurry-fused silicide', 'pack cementation'; 'reactive-element effect'; 'germanium-modified silicide' and 'boron-doped silicide' (glass-forming modifiers chosen in the 1960s precisely to lower scale viscosity and self-heal in the pest window — a trick the modern HEA literature mostly re-derives). Literatures to dig: AFML/WADD/AFFDL technical reports 1958-1972, NASA TN/TM and Lewis Research Center oxidation work, the Dyna-Soar / X-20 / ASSET / X-15 coating qualification programs, Battelle DMIC (Defense Metals Information Center) memoranda and Reviews, Bureau of Mines and Climax Molybdenum bulletins, Metallurgical Reviews on refractory metals, and INIS/IAEA translations of Soviet 'zharostoikie pokrytiya' reviews. TRAP: this field has a lot of modern Chinese silicide-coating papers; a scout must not return those. Also: the old reports' test atmospheres were air at 1 atm or crude low-pressure rigs, so a lead must be re-checked under realistic pO2 and water vapour, and some coatings were qualified only for single-mission ~minutes-to-hours lives. || WHY OLD LIT: Between 1958 and 1972 the US spent an enormous, mostly classified-then-declassified effort coating Nb and Mo for reusable hypersonic vehicles, generating thousands of cyclic-oxidation and pest-regime data points on hundreds of named coating formulations. The programs were cancelled with the vehicles, the formulations were never commercialised, and the reports are grey literature: scanned PDFs in DTIC/NTRS, outside Scopus/WoS, pre-digital-citation, so today's refractory-HEA community is effectively starting from zero on a solved sub-problem. The composition space searched then (Si-Cr-Fe, Si-Ge, Si-B, Si-Ti-Mo slurries) overlaps almost exactly what is being re-screened now. || HOW TO CHECK: Checkable at modest cost: pack-cementation or slurry-fuse the old recipe onto a C-103 or Nb-Si or RHEA coupon, then run isothermal + cyclic oxidation (box furnace or TGA, 700-900 C pest soaks and 1300-1500 C holds, 100+ cycles) with mass-change, cross-sectional SEM/EDS and XRD. Standard capability at any high-temperature materials lab; weeks to a few months. A document-level check is even cheaper: confirm the old report's reported cycles-to-failure and compare directly with the best published modern coating under matched conditions.

targets.problem: Driving PFAS all the way to inorganic fluoride at low energy and at realistic concentrations/matrices, instead of stalling at short-chain C2-C4 intermediates. Hydrated-electron and plasma routes consistently plateau (perfluoro radicals recombine to dimers rather than take another electron); incineration is still the baseline; the headline near-complete-defluorination results (Li-metal-mediated electrochemistry, ZnS photocatalysis) are preprints/abstracts on spiked clean water. The specific stuck sub-problem: a reducing system with the electron-transfer potential and fluoride-sequestering medium to cleave the last, most electron-poor C-F bonds.
targets.notes: B-terms: 'defluorination of fluorocarbons' by alkali metals, 'sodium naphthalenide' / 'sodium-ammonia (Birch-type) reduction of fluorocarbons', 'sodium amalgam', 'alkali-metal/molten-alkali attack on PTFE', 'Na-naphthalene etchant' (the standard industrial PTFE surface-activation chemistry — it defluorinates Teflon at room temperature, which is the hardest C-F substrate there is); 'Tetra-Etch'; 'fluorocarbon degradation over heated iron/nickel'; 'defluorination over carbon catalyst'; molten hydroxide/carbonate 'alkali fusion' and the old halide-analysis literature (combustion in a Parr bomb with Na2O2 was routine quantitative total-fluorine chemistry by 1950); Soviet work in Zhurnal Obshchei Khimii / Izvestiya on perfluoroalkyl reductions, and the Nesmeyanov-school organofluorine volumes. Literatures to dig: Journal of Fluorine Chemistry pre-1985, Advances in Fluorine Chemistry, Fluorine Chemistry Reviews, DuPont/3M/ICI patents 1950-1975, plus adhesion/surface-science literature on PTFE etching, which the environmental community does not cite at all. VERIFIED GAP: a general web search for the 1950s-60s alkali-metal fluorocarbon reduction work surfaced essentially nothing — it is not in the search-engine-visible layer the current PFAS field reads. TRAP: a lead must come with a plausible route to AQUEOUS or dilute operation, or at least a concentrate-then-destroy pairing; 'burn it in molten sodium' is not news, so the find must be a specific mediator, electron-shuttle, or fluoride-acceptor that lowers the energy or lets the chemistry run near ambient. || WHY OLD LIT: The organofluorine industry had to destroy, analyse and surface-activate perfluorocarbons for decades, and developed reductive C-F cleavage chemistries that work on PTFE itself. That work was published for synthesis, analysis and adhesion purposes, in journals and patents that predate the environmental-PFAS field by fifty years, with zero citation overlap: the modern field's vocabulary ('PFAS', 'mineralization', 'remediation') did not exist, and the old vocabulary ('fluorocarbon', 'defluorination', 'etchant') is not what anyone searches. Two literatures, same bond, no citations between them. || HOW TO CHECK: Directly testable at bench scale and relatively cheap: react the specified reductant/mediator with PFOA, PFOS and a short-chain (PFBA/PFBS) in the stated solvent, then measure defluorination by fluoride ion-selective electrode or ion chromatography and residual parent/intermediates by LC-MS/MS, with a total-organic-fluorine balance to prove mineralization rather than chain-shortening. Any environmental-chemistry lab, days to weeks per candidate; air-sensitive reductants need a glovebox or Schlenk line. The fluorine mass balance is the decisive check and is what most current preprints are weakest on.

targets.problem: Predicting and suppressing solidification/liquation (hot) cracking in additively manufactured alloys with wide freezing ranges — AA7075 and AA6061, and non-weldable gamma-prime Ni superalloys (IN738LC, CM247LC, Mar-M247). The field has process-specific escapes (Si additions, inoculant grain refinement, substrate preheating, smaller parts) but no transferable criterion: RDG and Kou indices mis-rank alloys, the role of grain-boundary misorientation and liquid-film stability is contested, and element loss by vaporisation (Zn, Mg) shifts susceptibility 16-21%. The stuck sub-problem: a quantitative susceptibility criterion that works across alloys, plus compositional fixes that do not destroy the alloy's reason for existing.
targets.notes: B-terms: 'hot shortness', 'hot tearing', 'crater cracking', 'microfissuring', 'strain-age cracking', 'liquation cracking', 'the brittle temperature range (BTR)', 'ductility-dip'; 'Borland's generalised theory', 'Prokhorov criterion', 'Medovar', 'Pellini's shrinkage-brittleness theory', 'Bochvar', 'Singer and Jennings'; 'Houldcroft ring test', 'varestraint / Varestraint test', 'circular-patch test', 'fishbone test', 'Trans-Varestraint' — a whole quantitative testing apparatus with published BTR curves for hundreds of compositions; and 'eutectic healing' / 'backfilling'. Also 'electroslag', 'electron-beam welding of refractory metals', and continuous-casting 'hot tear' literature in steel (an adjacent field with its own vocabulary and no citation link to AM). Literatures to dig: Welding Journal Research Supplement and British Welding Journal 1950-1980; Avtomaticheskaya Svarka / Automatic Welding (Paton Institute) in translation; Metal Construction; Journal of the Iron and Steel Institute on hot tearing; AFS casting literature on hot tears in permanent-mould Al. Note the thermal-condition mismatch: AM cooling rates are 10^3-10^6 K/s vs weld/casting 10^0-10^2, so an old criterion has to be re-derived, not copy-pasted — that is a real caveat, not a disqualifier. TRAP: confirmed by search that modern AM hot-cracking papers do NOT cite Borland/Prokhorov; do not accept a 'find' that is just a modern paper rediscovering the BTR concept, and do not count weldability-chart folk knowledge (Al-Si crack-sensitivity curves) as novel. || WHY OLD LIT: Welding and casting metallurgy solved large parts of this problem between 1940 and 1980 with standardised mechanical tests that measured the brittle temperature range directly, and built theory about liquid-film continuity, grain-boundary wetting and eutectic backfill. The AM community grew out of mechanical/manufacturing engineering and laser physics rather than welding metallurgy, and a search of recent AM cracking papers confirms the founding criteria are largely uncited; much of the source material is in Welding Journal supplements and Soviet welding journals from before the online citation era. || HOW TO CHECK: Two-stage and affordable. First a pure computation: take an old BTR dataset or criterion, recompute susceptibility rankings with Scheil/CALPHAD for the specific AM alloys, and see whether it ranks the known crack-prone/crack-free AM alloys better than RDG or Kou — a weekend of compute, no lab needed. Then a physical check: print single-track and small-wall specimens on an existing LPBF/DED machine with the old literature's prescribed fix (specific inoculant, minor-element addition, or thermal condition) and count cracks by metallography and X-ray CT. One printing campaign, a few weeks on existing equipment.

targets.problem: A methanol-synthesis catalyst that tolerates the water-rich, CO2-rich feed of green/e-methanol plants. The industrial Cu/ZnO/Al2O3 catalyst was optimised for CO-rich syngas; on CO2+H2 every molecule of methanol makes a molecule of water, and the catalyst deactivates by Cu sintering, hydrothermal particle aggregation/densification and (per 2025 operando XRD at 184-331 bar) carbonation of ZnO to ZnCO3 in the acidic CO2-saturated aqueous medium. Deactivation mechanisms are still being argued about and there is no drop-in water-tolerant replacement; this is the single biggest catalyst risk in e-methanol scale-up.
targets.notes: B-terms: 'zinc chromite', 'ZnO-Cr2O3', 'high-pressure methanol synthesis', 'the 250-atmosphere process', 'BASF Mittasch catalyst', 'Zn-Cr-Mn', 'sulphur-resistant methanol catalyst'; 'methanol-higher-alcohol (methanol-isobutanol) synthesis'; 'water-gas shift over chromia'; 'steam ageing', 'hydrothermal sintering', 'steam treatment of copper catalysts'. OLD vocabulary note: pre-1966 everyone ran Zn-Cr at 250-350 bar and 350-400 C precisely BECAUSE it was robust to water, CO2 and sulphur — the whole point of the 1966 ICI low-pressure Cu catalyst switch was activity at the cost of that robustness, and the industry then stopped publishing on Zn-Cr. Literatures to dig: Industrial & Engineering Chemistry 1925-1960; the BIOS/FIAT/CIOS post-war intelligence reports on German high-pressure synthesis (Leuna/Ludwigshafen operating data, essentially uncited today); US Bureau of Mines synthetic-liquid-fuels reports; the Fischer-Tropsch Archive (fischer-tropsch.org) scans; Soviet Kinetika i Kataliz; Natta's chapter in Catalysis (Emmett, 1955). Adjacent-field angle: the higher-alcohol-synthesis DOE work of the 1980s-90s on promoted zinc chromite in slurry reactors sits in grey OSTI reports and is not read by the CO2-to-methanol community. TRAP: Cr(VI) toxicity is a real blocker for a literal Zn-Cr revival, so a usable lead is either (a) the structural/promoter principle that conferred hydrothermal stability, transferable to a Cr-free spinel or ZnAl2O4/ZnZrOx, or (b) specific old steam-stability data that reframes the modern 'water tolerance' target; and remember Zn-Cr needed high pressure and gave low per-pass activity, so claims must be compared at matched conditions. || WHY OLD LIT: There was a commercial methanol catalyst family that ran for forty years in exactly the hostile condition the modern catalyst fails in, and it was abandoned for activity and Cr toxicity rather than for stability. Its performance data live in pre-1960 journals, in captured-German-industry intelligence reports, and in Bureau of Mines bulletins — paper sources with essentially no citation path into today's CO2-hydrogenation literature, which treats water tolerance as a new problem. Independently confirmed by search: recent work on Cu/ZnO water deactivation does not engage the zinc-chromite record at all. || HOW TO CHECK: Well-posed and standard: synthesise the old formulation (or its Cr-free structural analogue), run CO2+H2 at 30-80 bar and 220-300 C in a fixed-bed microreactor with deliberate water co-feed, and compare space-time yield, selectivity and deactivation rate head-to-head against a commercial CZA charge over 100-500 hours, with Cu surface area (N2O titration) and XRD/TEM before and after. targets.problem: A continuous, high-current-efficiency electrolytic route from TiO2 or TiCl2 to titanium metal, to displace the batch Kroll process. FFC-Cambridge and its relatives remain batch and sub-industrial: the blockers named in the literature are the long, complex cathodic deoxygenation path (getting below ~1000-2000 ppm O), low current efficiency from electronic conduction/shuttling of mixed-valent Ti species in the melt, strict TiO2 feed-purity requirements, and anode durability (carbon anodes contaminate, oxygen-evolving and PGM-coated anodes are expensive or passivate). Kroll is still the baseline in 2025 and essentially all tonnage.
targets.notes: B-terms: 'electrowinning of titanium', 'fused-salt electrolysis', 'TiCl2/TiCl3 disproportionation', 'subhalide', 'diaphragm cell', 'bipolar/anode-current-efficiency loss by valence cycling' (the old literature's phrase for the shuttle problem), 'Kroll-Bureau of Mines cell', 'Dow-Howmet', 'TIMET electrolytic cell', 'New Jersey Zinc process', 'Horizons cell', 'Ti cathode deposit harvesting / dendritic deposit', 'calcium-thermic and calcium-chloride deoxidation', 'Ca-CaCl2 flux deoxidation' (the OS/calciothermic ancestor), 'titanium carbosulphide / carbonitride soluble anode'. Literatures to dig: Bureau of Mines Reports of Investigation and Bulletins on titanium 1948-1970 (very large; several pilot electrolytic cells were actually operated); Journal of the Electrochemical Society and Transactions of AIME 1950-1975; Electrochimica Acta on molten-salt Ti; Soviet molten-salt electrochemistry (Baimakov, Smirnov, 'Elektrometallurgiya tsvetnykh metallov', Rasplavy journal), much of it only in Russian or in Freund/Consultants-Bureau translation; also the uranium/zirconium/rare-earth electrowinning literature from the AEC, which solved analogous mixed-valence-shuttle and dendrite-harvesting problems under a different metal's name. TRAP: Kroll's cost advantage is from decades of scale, so a lead has to be more than 'it worked in a lab cell' — look specifically for reported current efficiency, oxygen content achieved, cell life, and HOW the deposit was harvested continuously, since harvesting and salt carryover, not the reduction itself, is the usual killer. Also do not re-report FFC/Metalysis/OS/USTB processes; those are the incumbents of this target. || WHY OLD LIT: Multiple industrial players (Bureau of Mines, Dow, New Jersey Zinc, Horizons, TIMET) ran titanium electrolytic pilot cells in the 1950s-60s and solved specific engineering sub-problems — valence-shuttle suppression with diaphragms and redox buffers, continuous dendrite harvesting, salt recovery — then abandoned the work when Kroll sponge scaled and the Cold War titanium demand curve flattened. That record is almost entirely paper-era government and corporate grey literature, pre-digital and uncited by the FFC-era academic field, which has largely re-derived the same obstacles under new names. Search confirms the modern reviews frame oxygen removal and current efficiency as the live barriers without reference to that pilot-plant record. || HOW TO CHECK: Mixed cost but partly checkable for free. Document-level first: a surviving lead is a specific cell geometry, melt composition, redox buffer, or harvesting scheme with reported current efficiency and final oxygen content — that can be compared on paper against published FFC/OS numbers immediately, and screened thermodynamically (Ti-O-Cl-Ca activity and electronic-conductivity estimates) with no hardware. Physical validation needs a molten-salt electrochemistry lab: a 100 g to 1 kg CaCl2/NaCl-KCl cell at 700-900 C, inert atmosphere, measuring current efficiency by mass balance and oxygen by LECO combustion. Months and a real lab, but these cells exist in a dozen groups worldwide, and the first hint of a result is the oxygen number alone.

targets.problem: Rechargeable zinc anodes (both alkaline Zn-air/Ni-Zn and the newer mild-electrolyte aqueous Zn-ion cells) still fail by dendrite penetration and by 'shape change' — net redistribution of zinc from electrode edges toward the center over cycling, which strands active material and kills capacity. Lab fixes reach hundreds of cycles at favorable DoD/current density; nothing reliably reaches the thousands of deep cycles grid storage needs. Specifically: what additive/separator/current-waveform combination suppresses shape change at >50% zinc utilization and >10 mA/cm2?
targets.notes: B-terms to bridge through: zinc densification, 'shape change', electrode slumping, convective electrolyte flow in zincate, zincate supersaturation, hydrogen overvoltage additives, 'anodic passivation of zinc in KOH'. OLD vocabulary: 'zincate ion transport', 'secondary alkaline zinc cell', 'silver-zinc cell' (the aerospace/submarine literature), 'shape change in sealed nickel-zinc cells', 'inorganic separator', 'Emulphogene/organic surfactant inhibitor', 'pulse charging / asymmetric AC superimposed charge'. Literatures to dig: NASA Lewis/Goddard contractor reports and Yardney/Gould/ESB/Eagle-Picher technical reports 1965-1985 on Ag-Zn and Ni-Zn for aerospace and EV programs (vast, almost never cited by the 2015+ aqueous-Zn-ion community); Soviet/Japanese electrochemistry journals of the same era; electrowinning/electroplating literature on leveling agents and throwing power; IEEE/SAE EV-battery proceedings 1975-82. Verified live 2025: current papers still frame dendrite/shape-change as the limiting failure mode and report only partial, high-current-density-limited fixes. || WHY OLD LIT: Rechargeable alkaline zinc was an industrial program for ~25 years (aerospace silver-zinc, Ni-Zn EV prototypes) and was abandoned for reasons of cost/mercury/competition with Li-ion, not because the engineering was unpublished. Days per candidate, standard electrochemistry equipment. A surviving lead that holds up in the half-cell can then go into a pouch cell with an air electrode to check the poisoning question.

targets.problem: Mixed-halide (Br/I) wide-bandgap perovskite absorbers — the top cell in every tandem roadmap — segregate under illumination into I-rich and Br-rich domains within minutes, pinning the voltage and, under sustained 1-sun, losing I2 irreversibly at the surface. There is still no accepted mechanism ranking (photo-generated-carrier-driven halide migration vs. defect/vacancy-mediated diffusion vs. surface chemistry) and no composition/dopant strategy that stops it at the bandgaps tandems need (~1.7-1.8 eV).
targets.notes: B-terms to bridge through: photolytic halide decomposition, iodine/interstitial-halide Frenkel defects, photo-induced ionic conduction in a semiconducting ionic solid, 'latent image' / photolytic silver speck formation, halide vacancy diffusion, deep-trap dopants, photochromism and photo-bleaching, halide-ion polarizability. OLD vocabulary: 'photographic sensitivity', 'photolysis of silver halides', 'latent image formation', 'Gurney-Mott mechanism', 'interstitial silver ion mobility', 'chemical sensitization / sulfur sensitization', 'iridium and rhodium doping as electron traps', 'print-out effect', 'photochromic glass darkening/fading kinetics', 'F-centres and colour centres in alkali halides'. Literatures to dig: photographic science 1930-1980 (Mees, James's 'Theory of the Photographic Process', Journal of Photographic Science, Photographic Science and Engineering, Kodak and Ilford research reports); color-centre physics in alkali and lead halides (Seitz, Mott-Gurney 'Electronic Processes in Ionic Crystals'); photochromic silver-halide glass (Corning, 1960s-70s) on reversible-vs-irreversible photolysis and on how dopants control fade kinetics; also pre-1985 work on PbI2 and PbBr2 photoconductors/photodetectors. These fields solved, quantitatively, exactly the problem of 'light drives ions in a halide lattice and nucleates a new phase' — including which trace dopants suppress it — and the perovskite literature essentially never cites them. TRAP: the loose analogy 'perovskites are like film' is sometimes hand-waved in reviews; the deliverable must be a SPECIFIC transferable prescription (a named dopant at a named level, a named sensitizer/desensitizer class, or a quantitative nucleation model with parameters), not the analogy. Verified live: 2025 EES/Chem Sci papers report new migration modes, separate reversible segregation from irreversible I2 loss, and a 2026 preprint still treats the thermodynamics as unsettled. || WHY OLD LIT: Photographic science was an enormous, industrially funded, highly quantitative discipline about photo-driven ion migration and phase nucleation in halide crystals, and it went extinct as a field in the 1990s with digital imaging — its journals are poorly digitized, its vocabulary ('desensitizer', 'print-out') shares no keywords with perovskite papers, and the two communities have no citation path. Photochromic-glass work has the same shape: it is engineering literature about tuning reversibility of halide photolysis with dopants. || HOW TO CHECK: Highly checkable: fabricate wide-bandgap perovskite films with the candidate old-literature dopant/additive and run standard photoluminescence-shift and XRD-peak-splitting tests for segregation under 1-sun, plus voltage stability in a device. Standard perovskite lab, weeks, low cost. A negative result is equally informative, and a documentary pre-check (does the photographic literature's measured activation energy for interstitial halide motion match perovskite values?) costs nothing.

targets.problem: In Hanford low-activity-waste vitrification, Tc-99 is semi-volatile at melter temperature: roughly two-thirds leaves the melt into the offgas, single-pass glass retention averages ~35%, and the flowsheet copes by recycling offgas condensate back through the melter indefinitely. No chemistry has been found that holds Tc in the melt on a single pass. The specific problem: a feed additive, redox control, or melt chemistry that converts volatile Tc(VII) species into a non-volatile form that incorporates into borosilicate glass before the volatilization window.
targets.notes: B-terms: pertechnetate volatility, Tc2O7 vapor pressure, rhenium as surrogate (Re2O7 volatility), sulfate partitioning and salt-layer formation, redox buffering of the melt (Fe(II)/Fe(III)), reductant/getter additives, alkali-technetate stability, spinel/salt-phase capture. OLD vocabulary: 'roasting of molybdenite and recovery of rhenium', 'rhenium heptoxide fume', 'perrhenate scrubbing', 'volatilization losses in smelting', 'fume and flue-dust chemistry', 'oxide volatility in glass melting (selenium/boron/halide retention)', and 1950s-60s radiochemistry: 'technetium chemistry' (Boyd, Fried, Kotegov-era Soviet reviews), 'volatility of technetium heptoxide'. Literatures to dig: extractive-metallurgy literature on Re recovery from molybdenite roasting 1930-1980 (an entire industry built around predicting and controlling Re2O7 volatility from oxide melts and dusts — chemically the closest analogue to Tc and essentially uncited by the vitrification community); classical glass-technology literature on retaining volatile constituents in commercial glass melts (fluoride, selenium, boron) 1920-1980; early Oak Ridge/Argonne/Soviet technetium radiochemistry; and 1950s work on alkali perrhenates/pertechnetates and their thermal stability. TRAP: PNNL has already done sulfate-partitioning and Re-surrogate studies, so screen against the existing PNNL/SRNL report body (PNNL-32344, OSTI 1254603, SRNL-STI-2017-00087 and later) before claiming anything new; the seam is the non-nuclear metallurgy and glass-technology literature. Verified live: DOE/PNNL reports through 2025 still treat Tc retention as an active flowsheet problem addressed by recycle, not by chemistry. || WHY OLD LIT: The chemistry of controlling an extremely volatile Group-7 heptoxide out of a hot oxide melt was solved commercially for rhenium by metallurgists decades before anyone needed to immobilize Tc-99, and those two literatures share no journals, no keywords ('fume loss' vs 'melter retention') and no citation path. Much of it is pre-1960 metallurgical-society transactions and non-English. || HOW TO CHECK: Very checkable, and cheap at first: crucible melts of LAW simulant with Re as the non-radioactive surrogate plus the candidate additive, measuring Re retention against the published baseline — this is already a routine PNNL/SRNL protocol, so a lead plugs straight into an existing test rig. Scale-up to a lab-scale continuous melter if the crucible result holds. Even a documentary result is actionable: a cited mechanism would redirect a program with a multi-billion-dollar flowsheet riding on it.

targets.problem: Salt-hydrate thermal storage (Na2SO4-10H2O, CaCl2-6H2O, Na2S2O3-5H2O, CH3COONa-3H2O) — the cheapest dense heat storage available, and the one that would make building-scale load shifting economic — is still blocked by two 1950s problems: deep supercooling (nucleation-limited, so the stored heat does not come back at the design temperature) and incongruent melting/phase separation (lower hydrate settles out, capacity fades over cycles). Nucleator selection remains empirical, and no combination demonstrates thousands of stable cycles. Specific question: a predictive rule (lattice-match/isomorphism based) for choosing a nucleator, plus a congruency fix that survives long cycling.
targets.notes: B-terms: heterogeneous nucleation, lattice matching / isomorphism of the nucleant, 'seed crystal retention', thickening agents and thixotropic suspension to prevent segregation, extra-water principle, 'cold finger' nucleation, borax as nucleant, undercooling kinetics. OLD vocabulary: 'Glauber's salt heat-of-fusion storage', 'latent heat storage for solar space heating', 'eutectic salt storage', 'phase separation in Glauber salt', 'Telkes', 'thixotropic Glauber salt', 'nucleating catalyst', 'rolling cylinder storage', 'incongruent melting of salt hydrates'. Literatures to dig: Maria Telkes's own work and the 1973-1985 solar-heating grey literature — ERDA/DOE, NSF-RANN, Sandia, NASA Lewis and University of Delaware 'Solar One' reports, International Solar Energy Society proceedings, Dow Chemical and Calor Group technical reports — which screened hundreds of nucleator/thickener combinations with long cycle tests that are not in modern databases; plus classical crystallization literature (Mullin, Nyvlt; industrial crystallization of sulfates and chlorides) on nucleant lattice-match rules; plus the cloud-seeding/ice-nucleation literature 1947-1980 (silver iodide and organic ice nucleants: an entire quantitative theory of 'which solid nucleates which crystal, and why', built on epitaxial lattice match, developed with no contact with heat storage); plus food-science and pharmaceutical hydrate/polymorph literature on seeding and hydrate stability. TRAP: borax-on-Glauber-salt and SrCl2-on-CaCl2 are already standard; the 2024 ORNL-linked review already compiles ~38 nucleator/salt pairs, so a scout must diff against that review. The live seams are the cloud-seeding nucleation rules and the long-cycle-test data buried in 1970s solar reports. Verified live: 2023-2025 reviews still list pronounced supercooling, severe phase separation and poor cycling stability as the critical barriers. || WHY OLD LIT: The US solar-heating push of the 1970s funded an enormous empirical program on exactly these salts, and it was published as agency contractor reports and conference proceedings that are now scanned PDFs at best — uncited, unindexed, and using terms ('Glauber's salt', 'thixotropic') the modern PCM literature does not search for. Independently, ice-nucleation science built the predictive lattice-match theory the PCM field says it lacks, for a different purpose. || HOW TO CHECK: Among the cheapest targets to check. A DSC/thermocouple test of the salt plus candidate nucleator/thickener measures the supercooling depth immediately, and a 500-1000 cycle thermal-cycling rig (cheap, buildable) tests congruency. Days for a first screen, weeks for the cycling, materials costing tens of dollars. A documentary check comes first: do the 1970s reports already contain cycle-stability data better than today's published best?

targets.problem: As inverter-based resources displace synchronous machines, grids keep producing oscillatory instabilities that the standard analysis framework does not predict: subsynchronous control interaction with series-compensated lines, loss of equilibrium in grid-forming inverters under deep sags or high line impedance, and newly identified SSO pathways introduced by the sequence-decomposition that grid codes now mandate. Each event is diagnosed after the fact. Specific problem: a stability criterion for an inverter-dominated, low-short-circuit-ratio network that holds across the coupled 0.1-100 Hz band instead of the decoupled categories inherited from machine-era analysis.
targets.notes: B-terms: synchronizing and damping torque coefficients, negative damping, 'hunting', subsynchronous resonance and torsional interaction, induction generator effect, impedance-based (Nyquist) stability criterion, passivity of the terminal admittance, phase-margin design against a network impedance, equilibrium-point disappearance / loss of synchronism as a saddle-node bifurcation, describing-function and harmonic-balance analysis. OLD vocabulary: 'hunting of synchronous machines', 'self-excitation of induction machines', 'negative-resistance oscillation', 'HVDC converter-AC system interaction', 'commutation failure and harmonic instability', 'network analyzer (AC calculating board) studies', 'dynamic stability' as distinct from 'steady-state stability', 'Nyquist criterion applied to feedback amplifiers' / 'Bode phase-gain relation', 'torsional interaction with static exciters'. Literatures to dig: 1920s-40s AIEE transactions on machine hunting and on self-excited oscillation, where the physics of a converter-like source feeding a weak impedance was worked out with negative-damping arguments; the 1970-85 HVDC literature (Mojave, Square Butte, the 1970/1971 Mohave SSR shaft failures) — much of which already contains impedance-based criteria for an electronically controlled source destabilizing a compensated AC network; classic feedback/servomechanism theory (Nyquist, Bode, Nichols; MIT Radiation Lab series) on multi-loop and cross-coupled stability margins, which predates and generalizes the dq-frame cross-coupling results being published as new; and analog network-analyzer study reports from the utilities. TRAP: impedance-based stability analysis is already mainstream in the inverter literature (and already credited to Middlebrook-era power electronics), so returning 'use Nyquist' is worthless; the lead must be specific — a pre-1985 criterion, a stability-margin construction for cross-coupled loops, or documented HVDC-era mitigation (e.g. a specific damping filter/blocking topology) that maps onto a named modern GFM failure mode and is absent from today's citations. Verified live: 2025 IEEE papers report newly found SSO pathways; an Oct-2025 research talk lists preventing IBR-induced instabilities as open; IEC TR 63401-1 treats low-SCR oscillatory stability as unresolved. || WHY OLD LIT: The machine era solved a structurally identical problem — a controlled energy source interacting with a weak, compensated network across a band where mechanical, electrical and control dynamics couple — and wrote it up in AIEE/IEEE transactions, utility network-analyzer reports and HVDC commissioning studies using vocabulary ('hunting', 'negative damping', 'dynamic stability') that the inverter-stability literature does not search. The 1970s HVDC/SSR community in particular had hard-won, field-validated mitigation practice that is now mostly cited only for the SSR cases themselves, not for its general criteria. || HOW TO CHECK: Checkable by computation alone, which makes it unusually cheap: reconstruct the old criterion, apply it to a published GFM/weak-grid case that goes unstable in a modern EMT model (PSCAD/EMTP, or an open ERCOT-style series-compensated test system), and see whether it predicts the instability boundary the modern framework missed. Days to weeks of simulation, no hardware. A strong lead can then be tested on a controller-hardware-in-the-loop bench at a national lab.

targets.problem: Selenate (Se VI) removal to the single-digit microgram-per-litre limits now demanded of FGD wastewater and mining discharge. Selenate is kinetically inert, chemically mimics the thousands of mg/L of co-present sulfate, and the only commercially proven route (anoxic biological reduction to elemental Se) is capital- and operator-intensive, upset-prone, and degrades when dibasic acid or oxidants shift speciation back to selenate.
targets.notes: B-terms to bridge through: selenosulfate chemistry (sulfite dissolving elemental Se, reversibly); selenate reduction by dithionite/hydrazine/hypophosphite; microbial methylation to dimethyl selenide; selenate sorption on hydrous ferric and alumina phases at defined pH; sulfate-selenate coprecipitation. OLD VOCABULARY: 'seleniferous soils', 'alkali disease', 'blind staggers', 'selenium indicator plants', 'volatilization of selenium from soils', 'selenium in anode slimes', 'selenium rectifier', 'soda-ash roast of slimes', 'sulphite leach of selenium'. WHERE TO DIG: USDA/South Dakota Agricultural Experiment Station bulletins and Trelease & Beath, Moxon, Olson (1930s-1960s) on selenate mobility and biological volatilization; copper-refinery and selenium-metallurgy handbooks (Canadian Copper Refiners, Noranda practice) on selenosulfate and roast-leach chemistry; 1930s-60s analytical chemistry of selenium speciation. targets.problem: Construct a Hadamard matrix of order 668 (or 716, 892, 1132) — the smallest orders for which no Hadamard matrix is known, blocking the Hadamard conjecture's verified range. 668 = 4·167; 167 is prime, so none of the standard Paley/Sylvester/Williamson/Turyn families apply directly, and modern computer searches over Williamson-type and Goethals–Seidel arrays have not reached it.

Bulletin), 'orthogonal arrays' (Bose–Bush), 'skew-type matrices', 'Hadamard's determinant problem' (pre-WWII French/German), 'Jacobsthal matrices'. WHERE TO DIG: Sankhyā and the Calcutta Statistical Association Bulletin 1945–1980 (where much orthogonal/BIBD construction was published and never recrawled); Soviet combinatorics (Kibernetika, Problemy Peredachi Informatsii) under 'orthogonal codes'/'Mersenne-like signal sets'; 1960s–70s coding/radar engineering on 'binary sequences with zero periodic autocorrelation' (IEEE Trans. Inform. Theory, Aerospace), where SDS-equivalent objects were built for pulse compression without anyone noticing the design-theory implication; Baumert's 1971 Cyclic Difference Sets lecture notes and its uncited references. Also do not count modular/partial results: Eliahou's 2025 order-668 matrix is Hadamard only mod 64, not a real one. || WHY OLD LIT: The objects needed (supplementary difference sets on 167 points, base/Turyn sequences of specific lengths) were constructed by hand in the 1950s–70s inside statistics, radar signal design and Soviet coding theory, in journals that today's design-theory searches (which are code- and database-driven) do not index. The current standard reference is literally a database of constructions (arXiv:2411.18897), so any construction not in it is invisible. || HOW TO CHECK: Trivially and absolutely checkable: given a candidate 668×668 ±1 matrix, verify H·Hᵀ = 668·I — seconds of CPU. Given only a candidate SDS/sequence set from an old paper, plug into Goethals–Seidel and check the same identity. Cost: a scout plus minutes of compute. targets.problem: Minimum comparator COUNT for sorting networks on 13–17 channels. Size optimality is proven only up to n=12 (s(12)=39, Harder 2020). For n=13 the record is 45 comparators against a lower bound of 43; for n=16 the record is still Green's 60 from 1969 and has not been beaten in 57 years. Nobody knows whether 43/44 or 59 are achievable — exhaustive SAT search does not reach these n.
targets.notes: B-terms to bridge through: merge-exchange and odd–even merge schemes, Batcher merges with shared comparators, 'Green filters', Van Voorhis lower bound chains, (m,n)-merging networks M(m,n), selection networks U_t(n), partial-order / poset-based pruning, Boolean 0-1 principle. OLD VOCABULARY: 'comparator switching networks', 'sorting schemes' (skhemy sortirovki), 'rearrangeable switching networks', 'contact networks' / 'relay-contact schemes' (kontaktnye skhemy — Shannon 1938, then a huge Soviet literature: Lupanov, Yablonskii, Kuznetsov), 'minimal relay networks', 'threshold logic' and 'majority networks', 'permutation networks' (Benes, Waksman, Clos), 'bitonic sorters', 'minimum-exchange sorting' in early OR/punched-card literature. WHERE TO DIG: Problemy Kibernetiki and Diskretnyi Analiz 1960–1980 for minimal-comparator schemes on small n (small-n hand optimization was a Soviet specialty and results were stated as switching-network sizes, not sorting networks); Bell System Technical Journal 1950s–60s on rearrangeable networks; Knuth TAOCP vol. 3 §5.3.4 exercises and their original sources (Shapiro, Green, Van Voorhis, Juillé), several of which cite unpublished memoranda worth chasing; early IBM/Burroughs technical reports and US patents on hardware sorters (patents are a disconnected literature that never cites TCS). TRAP: do not confuse DEPTH with SIZE — depth optimality for 11≤n≤17 is largely settled (Bundala–Závodný and later), and a 2025 depth-13/28-channel result will keep surfacing in searches. Also beware of networks that only sort in the 'merge' sense or require a presorted prefix. || WHY OLD LIT: Small-n comparator networks were designed by hand in switching theory, telephony and hardware-sorter engineering for twenty years before the TCS community standardized on 'sorting networks'. Those designers were minimizing contacts/gates, i.e. exactly comparator count, on exactly the small n that matter here, and published in Russian-language cybernetics journals and in patents — neither of which current SAT-based papers cite. That Green's 1969 network has resisted 57 years of modern search is itself evidence the good constructions came from a design tradition that has since been forgotten. || HOW TO CHECK: Exact and cheap. A candidate network on n channels is a correct sorting network iff it sorts all 2^n 0-1 inputs (Knuth's zero-one principle): n=17 is 131072 bitmask tests, microseconds. So any comparator list extracted from a 1965 Russian paper or a 1971 patent diagram is verified in a single short script, and if it beats the record it is immediately publishable with a machine certificate.

targets.problem: Is the tensor rank of 3×3 matrix multiplication less than 23? Laderman's 23-multiplication scheme (1976) is still the best known upper bound; the best general lower bound is 19 (Bläser). Fifty years, thousands of inequivalent rank-23 schemes found, zero rank-22, no proof of optimality over general fields. The same gap exists for other small formats (3×3×4, 3×4×4, 4×4 beyond Strassen-squared, and partial/rectangular products) where current practical fast-matmul libraries are stuck.
targets.notes: B-terms to bridge through: trilinear aggregation / aggregating-cancelling-uniting (APA), border rank and degeneration, pencils of matrices and Kronecker normal form, Hopcroft–Kerr commutative/noncommutative distinction, disjoint partial matrix multiplication, substitution method, Alder–Strassen bound, group-algebra and Hadamard-product embeddings. OLD VOCABULARY: 'bilinear forms complexity' / 'slozhnost' vychisleniya bilineinykh form', 'aggregation of computations', 'trilinear aggregating' (V. Ya. Pan, 1972–1984, much of it in Russian and in translated-but-unread venues), 'Kronecker/Weierstrass theory of matrix pencils' (1890s–1930s German literature on pairs of bilinear forms, Dickson, Kronecker, Weierstrass), 'canonical forms of pairs of bilinear forms', 'invariant theory of 3×3×3 trilinear forms' (classical invariant theory of cubic forms in three sets of variables — this literally classified the orbit structure of the 3×3×3 tensor space long before anyone cared about matmul), 'systems of bilinear identities', 'theory of composition algebras' (Hurwitz, Radon, Eckmann — gave minimal bilinear identities for sums of squares and products). WHERE TO DIG: Pan's Soviet-era papers and their bibliographies; Doklady/Izvestiya and Zh. Vychisl. Mat. i Mat. Fiz. 1972–1985; the classical invariant-theory literature on trilinear forms and the Kronecker–Weierstrass pencil classification; also algebraic-geometry papers on secant varieties of Segre varieties from the Italian school (Palatini, Terracini, 1900s–1920s) which computed defectivity and dimensions of exactly the varieties whose points are low-rank tensors. TRAP: heavily searched by brute force and by ML (AlphaTensor and successors), so do NOT propose another numeric search — the lead must be a structural identity or a dimension/orbit argument from the old literature. Also note the recent arXiv activity (2026) is about reducing ADDITION counts in rank-23 schemes and about F_2-specific lower bounds (≥20, ≥21 claimed), not about rank 22 over general fields; don't mistake those for a resolution. || WHY OLD LIT: Classical invariant theory and the Kronecker–Weierstrass theory of matrix pencils solved orbit-classification problems for small trilinear forms using methods that the modern complexity literature does not read, and Terracini-era Italian geometry computed secant-variety dimensions that directly bound border rank. On the construction side, Pan's trilinear-aggregation machinery produced explicit schemes for many small formats; much of that catalogue was never transcribed into machine-checkable form, so an unimplemented Pan-style aggregation for a small format may already beat what current libraries use. || HOW TO CHECK: Perfectly checkable: a candidate bilinear scheme is a set of rank-1 triples; verify the tensor identity symbolically (or over a random prime field with high confidence, then exactly) in seconds. A border-rank or orbit-dimension lead is checkable with a Gröbner/numerical-algebraic-geometry computation. Cost: a scout plus a laptop. Payoff: either a 50-year record or a concretely faster small-format kernel usable in real linear algebra.

targets.problem: Exact values of K_3(n,1), the football pool problem: the minimum number of ternary length-n words whose radius-1 Hamming balls cover {0,1,2}^n. Exact only to n=6 (=73). n=7 sits at 156–186 and has barely moved since the 1990s–2011; n=8 at 402–486. The same stall affects mixed/q-ary covering codes K_q(n,R) tables generally, which feed real applications (test-suite covering arrays, index coding, fault diagnosis).
targets.notes: B-terms to bridge through: 1-perfect and quasi-perfect codes, 'systems' for football pools, Steiner-like partial coverings, mixed covering codes, ADS (amalgamated direct sum) and blockwise direct sum constructions, matrix/piecewise-constant constructions, group-divisible designs, dominating sets in Hamming graphs K_3^n, 'surjective/covering arrays'. OLD VOCABULARY: 'reduced systems' and 'tipsystem'/'tippsystem'/'reduserte systemer' in Scandinavian recreational and statistical journals; 'Toto systems' (German/Hungarian/Italian), 'Lotto and Toto design', 'Nordisk Matematisk Tidskrift' and Norwegian/Swedish/Finnish pool-betting pamphlets 1947–1975; in design theory, 'covering designs' and 'Turán systems' (Turán's hypergraph covering problem, Katona–Nemetz–Simonovits, Hungarian literature 1960s); in engineering, 'diagnostic test sets', 'fault dictionaries', 'maintenance checkout schedules' (1950s–60s reliability and aircraft-maintenance literature, where covering sets of ternary states were tabulated under 'minimum checkout sets'). Kéri's online bounds table is the current authority and should be diffed against anything found. Meanwhile the modern attack is SDP/LP lower bounds plus simulated annealing upper bounds — nobody is reading 1958 Norwegian pool pamphlets, and a single good explicit system there drops an upper bound. || HOW TO CHECK: Instant and total: a claimed covering of size m for n=7 is 2187 words to check against m balls — milliseconds. targets.problem: Hardest-to-round bounds for correctly-rounded transcendental functions where exhaustive search is impossible: the bivariate cases (pow, atan2, hypot, compound) in binary64, and essentially all functions in binary128/decimal128. The Table Maker's Dilemma is now solved for UNIVARIATE binary64 by exhaustive Lefèvre-style search (Lefèvre–Ly–Zimmermann completed sin/cos/tan), but those methods do not scale: for binary128 the search space is ~2^113 and for pow the domain is 2^128, so correctly-rounded libm work (CORE-MATH, IEEE 754-2019's recommended operations) is blocked on an ANALYTIC bound on how many identical bits can follow the round bit.
targets.notes: B-terms to bridge through: effective measures of transcendence and irrationality, linear forms in logarithms with explicit constants, |e^x − p/q| and |x^y − p/q| lower bounds for rational/dyadic x,y, Mahler's classification and S-numbers, continued-fraction/three-distance arguments for x·log2(e), Baker's theorem with explicit constants, Gel'fond–Schneider effective versions, p-adic analogues, hypergeometric Padé/Thue–Siegel methods, exponential-sum estimates for the distribution of hard cases. OLD VOCABULARY: 'mera transtsendentnosti' (measure of transcendence), 'approximation of logarithms of algebraic numbers by rational numbers', 'Gel'fond's method', 'Fel'dman's estimates', 'effektivnye otsenki' — a very large Soviet Diophantine-approximation literature (Gel'fond, Fel'dman, Shidlovskii, Sprindzhuk) from 1935–1980 that computed explicit, usable constants precisely because pre-computer number theory cared about effectivity; plus Mahler's 1930s–50s papers giving concrete bounds on |e^x − p/q| and on decimal expansions of transcendentals, and the Thue–Siegel–Baker 'explicit constants' tradition. WHERE TO DIG: Izvestiya AN SSSR Ser. Mat. and Mat. Zametki 1950–1980 under transcendence measures; Mahler's collected papers; Fel'dman–Shidlovskii surveys; also 1950s–60s numerical-analysis literature (Hart et al. Computer Approximations, Cody–Waite, NBS tables, and the Soviet 'tablichnye metody') where the table makers themselves reasoned about worst cases by hand. TRAP: searches will insist the TMD is 'solved' — that is only univariate binary64; state the target as bivariate/binary128 or it looks already done. Also: a transcendence measure that is effective but astronomically weak proves nothing useful, so the lead must be an explicit constant of practical size, and dyadic-rational arguments are ALGEBRAIC, so pure-transcendence statements may not apply — the needed statement is about x^y and e^x at dyadic points. || WHY OLD LIT: The computer-arithmetic community states this as an open problem and works around it probabilistically; the Diophantine-approximation community produced explicit effective bounds on exactly these quantities decades earlier for entirely unrelated reasons, and the two literatures barely cite each other (Lefèvre/Muller cite a handful of Baker-era results at most). Pre-1985 Soviet work emphasized explicit constants in a way modern transcendence theory, which prefers asymptotic statements, does not — making it an unusually good reservoir for a usable bound. || HOW TO CHECK: Checkable in layers and cheaply: (1) any claimed explicit bound can be stress-tested against the already-computed exhaustive worst-case lists for univariate binary64 (Lefèvre/Zimmermann's published tables) — if the bound is violated by a known worst case, the lead is dead in minutes; (2) if it survives, instantiate it for binary128 or pow and compare against randomized searches over hard cases; (3) the final artifact is a concrete, machine-checkable precision bound that CORE-MATH can adopt, i.e. a real code change, and the statement is formalizable in a proof assistant.

targets.problem: The Kolmogorov–Arnold-network program needs an exact or near-exact superposition representation with SMOOTH inner functions and quantitative approximation rates; Vitushkin's obstruction says exact Kolmogorov representation fails in C^k for k≥1, and the Demb–Sprecher question of whether the superpositions can be smoothed while keeping exactness is explicitly recorded as unanswered. Consequence: KANs have no usable rate theory, their widths/depths are set empirically, and 'KAN = universal approximator' arguments are either vacuous (Kolmogorov with non-smooth inner functions, uncomputable in practice) or unproved.
targets.notes: B-terms to bridge through: Sprecher's explicit inner function and its monotone-Cantor-like construction, Fridman's Lipschitz inner functions, Lorentz's and Hedberg's variants, Kahane's and Doss's proofs, Vitushkin's entropy/variation-of-order argument and his 'linear superposition' invariants, Kolmogorov's ε-entropy of function classes, Bakhvalov's and Kurkova's rate results. OLD VOCABULARY: 'superposition of functions' / 'superpozitsiya funktsii', 'Hilbert's 13th problem', 'representation of functions of several variables by functions of fewer variables', 'nomography' and 'nomographic representability' (a whole pre-1960 engineering-mathematics literature on which multivariable functions can be drawn as alignment charts — this IS the superposition question, asked by nomographers: Ocagne, Kellogg, Warmus, and the Soviet nomography school), 'variation of a function of order k' (Vitushkin's invariant), 'ε-entropy', 'tabulation and interpolation of functions of several variables' (Soviet computational literature on storing multivariate tables, which optimized exactly the smooth-superposition tradeoff for memory reasons). WHERE TO DIG: Uspekhi Mat. Nauk and Doklady 1954–1975 on superpositions (Vitushkin, Arnold, Kolmogorov, Ostrand, Tikhomirov); the nomography literature 1900–1960 including Warmus's and Soviet texts; Soviet numerical-tabulation literature; Tikhomirov's work on widths and entropy, which gives the matching LOWER bounds a rate theory would need. TRAP: the modern KAN literature mostly cites a 1957 one-liner and Sprecher/Kurkova secondhand; a scout must read Vitushkin's actual obstruction, since several 'smooth KAN' claims quietly weaken exactness to approximation and are therefore not counterexamples. Also, there IS 2024–2025 activity (Samadi et al.; an explicit C²-smooth APPROXIMATE construction, arXiv 2508.04392) — the live gap is quantitative rates and the exactness-vs-smoothness boundary, not the bare existence question. || WHY OLD LIT: Nomography asked precisely 'which functions of several variables are superpositions of functions of one or two variables' for fifty years as an engineering drawing problem, and Soviet function-theory produced sharp entropy/variation invariants that bound what any superposition architecture can do. The deep-learning literature using KANs cites almost none of this, so a quantitative rate theorem — or a sharp impossibility result that would redirect the whole architecture — may already be in print under 'variation of order k' or 'nomographic representability'. || HOW TO CHECK: Two checks, both cheap. Mathematically: an old construction can be transcribed and its claimed smoothness/rate verified, and candidate rate theorems can be formalized or at least sanity-checked against Tikhomirov-style entropy lower bounds (if a claimed rate beats the entropy bound, the lead is wrong — a one-page check). Computationally: implement the old explicit inner functions as the activation basis of a KAN layer and measure approximation error versus width on benchmark targets, against standard B-spline KANs — a few GPU-hours, and a win is directly publishable as an architecture change.

targets.problem: Laboratory-measured dissolution rates of silicate minerals (feldspars, olivine, basalt glass) exceed field-inferred weathering rates by 2-5 orders of magnitude, and no mechanistic model closes the gap — current practice uses a fitted 'reactivity coefficient' or an empirical field-scaling factor. The gap now has direct money attached: enhanced rock weathering (ERW) CO2-removal projects must predict basalt dissolution rates in soils, and crediting registries have no validated way to convert lab kinetics into field CO2 removal.
targets.notes: B-terms to bridge through: leached/altered surface layers (a passivating amorphous or hydrated rind), secondary-mineral precipitation controlling fluid saturation state, reactive surface area vs BET area, and transport-limited vs surface-reaction-limited regimes. OLD vocabulary for these: 'glass durability', 'weathering of glass', 'leached layer', 'dealkalization', 'interdiffusion layer', 'hydrolytic class' (container/optical-glass industry, 1920s-1970s); 'base exchange' and 'zeolitization' (1900s-1950s soil chemistry); 'protective film' and 'passive layer' (metal/alloy corrosion literature); 'pozzolanic reaction' and 'alkali-silica reaction' (concrete chemistry, 1940s-1970s). Cross-field literatures that do not cite geochemistry: ASTM/Society of Glass Technology durability testing, nuclear waste-glass leaching (1950s-1970s AEC/Hanford/Harwell reports, which built quantitative layer-diffusion models), ceramic engineering, and pre-1950 agronomy on 'availability of potash from feldspar' and rock-powder fertilizers (Germany and India ran decades of field trials applying ground silicate rock to soil — essentially ERW experiments under a different name). Traps: do not conflate the lab-field gap with the well-known pH and surface-area dependencies; those are already modeled. Do not propose 'microbes do it' as the lead — it is a well-mined hypothesis. Also avoid the famous Panola Granite / Brantley line of work as a 'discovery'; it is the baseline, not the find. || WHY OLD LIT: The quantitative theory of a hydrated, diffusion-limiting surface layer on a silicate was worked out in glass science and nuclear-waste-glass programs decades before it was debated in geochemistry, in a vocabulary ('durability', 'dealkalization', 'hydrolytic class') that shares almost no keywords with 'dissolution rate' or 'weathering', so citation overlap is near zero. Separately, the agronomic rock-powder-fertilizer trials of roughly 1890-1960 contain multi-year field measurements of silicate release rates in real soils at real grain sizes, exactly the measurement ERW projects claim does not exist. || HOW TO CHECK: Cheap and concrete. (1) Digitize rate constants and layer-growth exponents from old glass-durability and waste-glass leaching papers, convert units, and test whether their layer-diffusion formulation predicts the observed field/lab ratio for feldspar and basalt glass — a desk computation, days of work. (2) Re-analyze the agronomic rock-dust field trials as ERW rate measurements: extract application rate, grain size, soil pH, duration, and measured base-cation release; compare against current ERW field-trial rates. (3) Direct check: run a standard flow-through dissolution experiment on basalt powder with and without the specific pre-treatment old glass papers say produces or strips the passivating layer (e.g. HF-stripping, controlled hydration ageing) and see if rates converge toward field values. Weeks of lab time, standard equipment.

targets.problem: Lightning initiates inside thunderclouds at measured peak electric fields of roughly 3-4 kV/cm/atm, about an order of magnitude below the ~29 kV/cm/atm conventional breakdown threshold of air. No mechanism is settled: fast positive breakdown from ice hydrometeors, hydrometeor field enhancement, relativistic runaway breakdown, and a 2025 photoelectric/X-ray feedback model are all live, and 2025 LOFAR observations report an 'ultra-slow-propagation' initiation class nobody predicted. Verified live: competing 2019-2026 papers, an active ERC project, and new ALOFT gamma-ray campaigns all still framing it as open.
targets.notes: B-terms to bridge through: corona and streamer inception from a stressed dielectric droplet or ice needle; the streamer-to-leader transition and its minimum stable field; space-charge-limited field enhancement around a conducting protrusion; hydrometeor deformation (Taylor-cone / Rayleigh instability of a charged drop); the role of water vapor and droplets in lowering effective breakdown strength. OLD vocabulary: 'inception gradient', 'critical corona onset', 'long air gap breakdown', 'positive leader', 'switching-impulse strength', 'point-plane gap', 'humidity correction factor', 'Townsend coefficient', 'Paschen', 'electrohydrodynamic disintegration of drops'. Cross-field literatures: high-voltage power engineering, which spent the 1930s-1970s measuring leader inception in meter-scale gaps, including the Les Renardieres Group reports (1972-1981) and CIGRE/IEEE transmission-line insulation work; gas-discharge physics (Loeb, Meek, Raether, Kaptsov); 1940s-1960s aircraft and aerospace 'precipitation static' and fuel-tank ignition work; Soviet-era Elektrichestvo and Zhurnal Tekhnicheskoi Fiziki discharge papers; and Rayleigh/Zeleny/Macky/Taylor drop-breakup work (Macky 1931 measured drop disintegration fields directly). Traps: the C.T.R. Wilson 1925 runaway-electron and Gurevich 1992 runaway-breakdown lineage are already thoroughly mined — do not resurface those as the find. Also avoid treating the laboratory 'long spark' as a settled analogue; the point is to mine its humidity, water-droplet and bundled-conductor inception data, which atmospheric electricity papers almost never cite. || WHY OLD LIT: Utilities needed to know the exact field at which air breaks down in the presence of rain, fog and wet insulators, because transmission-line design depended on it. They published tens of thousands of measurements, including explicit wet-condition and droplet-on-conductor inception gradients, in IEEE/AIEE Transactions, CIGRE reports and national lab reports — a literature whose citation graph barely touches JGR-Atmospheres. If any of those measurements show inception at fields near the observed thundercloud values under droplet or ice-needle geometry, the 'paradox' may be partly an artifact of using dry, clean-air breakdown as the benchmark. || HOW TO CHECK: (1) Document check first: pull the Les Renardieres reports and AIEE/IEEE wet-gap inception data, tabulate measured inception gradients as a function of humidity, droplet presence and electrode radius, and compare directly against balloon-sounding thundercloud field profiles. Pure library work. (2) Computation: feed those measured inception criteria into existing streamer-initiation models with realistic ice-crystal aspect ratios and see whether initiation becomes possible at 3-4 kV/cm/atm. (3) Experiment: a reduced-pressure chamber with a suspended ice needle or supercooled droplet pair, scaled to cloud-base pressure, testing an inception criterion taken from the old HV literature. Equipment already exists in several atmospheric-electricity and HV labs; a single student project.

targets.problem: Large rock avalanches (sturzstroms, >1e6 m3) travel with apparent friction coefficients far below the friction angle of their own debris, and after sixty years there is still no agreed mechanism: a 2024 modelling paper states plainly that no consensus exists and it is unclear whether one mechanism suffices. Candidates (acoustic fluidization, mechanical fluidization, dynamic fragmentation, thermal pressurization, trapped air, basal water) are mostly supported by idealized 2D simulations. Practical consequence: runout-zone hazard maps for alpine and glacial-retreat-exposed valleys are calibrated empirically on volume-vs-runout regressions with no physics, so they extrapolate badly to the largest and the newly destabilized cases.
targets.notes: B-terms to bridge through: vibration-induced reduction of effective wall and internal friction in dense granular media; gas-interstitial lubrication and deaeration time of a collapsing powder bed; dilatant shear and the critical state of a rapidly sheared grain bed; segregation and basal fines layers as a lubricating boundary. OLD vocabulary: 'bulk solids handling', 'flooding' and 'flushing' of a powder, 'aeration' and 'deaeration', 'bin flow' and 'arching', 'vibrated bed', 'air-float conveying', 'fluidization velocity', 'angle of internal friction under vibration', 'Jenike flow function', 'Janssen stress'. Cross-field literatures: chemical and powder-handling engineering (Powder Technology, Transactions of the Institution of Chemical Engineers, 1950s-1980s), which measured exactly how much a vibrating or slightly aerated powder loses shear strength; silo and hopper design literature (Jenike's 1961-1964 Utah bulletins); grain-elevator and coal-dust explosion engineering; soil dynamics / liquefaction under vibration in 1950s-1970s earthquake engineering; and snow-avalanche and powder-snow-flow literature (Swiss SLF reports, often in German, rarely cited by rock-mechanics papers). Traps: do not re-present Heim's Fahrboschung or the Melosh acoustic-fluidization model as the discovery — they are the established frame. Do not dress up 'it was wet' as novel. The valuable target is quantitative strength-loss-vs-vibration-amplitude data from powder engineering that could be dropped straight into the acoustic-fluidization parameterization, which currently has essentially free parameters. || WHY OLD LIT: Acoustic fluidization has stayed contested largely because its key parameter (how much effective friction drops for a given vibrational pressure amplitude in a dense, polydisperse, confined granular bed) has never been measured for geological materials. That exact measurement was a routine industrial problem for decades under the words 'vibrated bulk solids', in journals geomorphology does not cite. Likewise, deaeration-time measurements for collapsing powder beds bound the lifetime of trapped-air lubrication, a number the rock-avalanche debate argues about qualitatively. || HOW TO CHECK: (1) Extract friction-reduction-vs-vibration-amplitude and deaeration-time curves from the powder-engineering literature, rescale to rock-avalanche grain sizes, confining stresses and durations, and plug them into an existing depth-averaged runout model (e.g. a Voellmy/mu-I or Hergarten-type solver); check whether the resulting runouts match the documented inventory of rock-avalanche volume-runout pairs without further tuning. A computation, with a public dataset. (2) Experiment: a ring-shear or inclined-flume test on crushed rock with controlled vibration and controlled interstitial gas pressure, reproducing the old powder tests on geological material. Standard rock-mechanics lab kit. (3) Immediate database payoff: if a surviving lead works, it becomes a revised runout-envelope used in hazard mapping, a checkable edit to existing susceptibility maps.
